notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (support platform) evaluating Redwood Hosted API as primary path; interested in Dedicated once traffic grows.

Context and business need:
- Building a chat-first customer support agent embedded in their web app; agent handles triage, KB lookup, and automatic ticket updates via tool calls to their Jira instance.
- Current latency target: first-token <= 1.5s for webchat (hard SLO). Overall p50 < 400ms, p99 < 2s preferred. Streaming required for perceived speed.
- Peak workload: ~120-200 concurrent users during business peak; expected steady-state reqs/sec ~80-120, burst to 150+. Cost sensitivity: moderate — will trade some cost for reliability/latency but want actionable unit economics.

Technical requirements & preferences:
- Streaming with incremental tokens + tool calling (ticket create/update) is must-have.
- Want model pinning and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants during capacity constraints.
- Data residency: US only for customer data; retention 90 days.
- Auth: Okta SSO (SAML) for admin console; API keys for runtime.
- Audit: detailed request/response audit logs for support escalations and compliance.

POC plan discussed:
- 2-week Hosted API POC: implement streaming chat + one tool integration to create Jira tickets.
- Load test: simulated 150 concurrent chat sessions with ongoing KV/prefix caching to validate latency and cost.
- Success criteria: first-token median < 0.5s, 90% of first-tokens < 1.5s, correct tool-call reliability > 99.5%.

Commercial & procurement notes:
- Initial interest in Hosted to reduce onboarding friction; Dedicated evaluated for predictable throughput if POC scales.
- Budget: looking at $50k-$150k ARR band; wants clear delta between Hosted and Dedicated pricing (committed vs burst).
- Pricing conversation: scheduled 2025-10-05 with pricing team (Maya + Diego + Voyager finance).

Security/legal:
- Security team requires SOC2 summary, encryption at rest with KMS, SSO integration doc. Asked for sample Data Processing Agreement (DPA).
- Blocker: procurement will not sign without SOC2 doc + DPA reviewed by legal.

Recent quotes/snippets from calls:
- "We need streaming or customers drop off — perceived lag kills conversion." — Head of Product
- "First token latency is non-negotiable; sub-1.5s or we re-architect." — CTO

Action items (owner in parens):
- Ship Hosted API POC onboarding steps + quickstart keys (Maya).
- SE to run end-to-end load test script and share logs (Diego).
- Pricing proposal + Hosted vs Dedicated TCO (pricing team).
- Send SOC2 summary + DPA template (Security Ops).

Notes on benchmarking so far:
- Diego ran local microbenchmarks: single-region hosted streaming baseline shows p50 ~0.35s first-token, p90 ~0.9s, p99 ~1.8s on sampled traffic. Need to validate at scale and cross-region.
- Want integration test with real ticket payloads and KV cache warmup.

Risks/concerns:
- If hosted cannot guarantee 1.5s first-token on POC, Voyager will push to hybrid (Dedicated for high-volume routes).
- Procurement timeline tied to SOC2 — may delay close to Dec quarter.

Next meeting: 2025-10-05 pricing + POC kickoff.
